adjustment.analysis: Halloween has a noise-adjusted effect of x1.0, so no lift. Price increased 5.5% to $10.81, which historically correlates with a 15% price increase (2026-09-28) leading to a 36% drop (x0.63). A 5.5% increase likely causes ~x0.85. Supplier delivery warning adds supply risk, but no past data; downshift median slightly. No promotion, so no uplift. Combine: x0.85 × x1.0 = x0.85. Shrink toward 1.0 due to thin evidence and noise. Final median multiplier 0.92. Downside spread widened slightly for uncertainty. Confidence: medium.

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 35.0 | 5%-95%: 19.2 - 57.5 | 10%-90%: 21.5 - 54.6

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-44% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
